title: Produce substantial fat loss while preserving skeletal muscle and strength

concept.text: Improve the composition and functional consequences of drug-induced weight loss by preserving muscle. BELIEVE demonstrated substantially less DXA lean-mass loss with bimagrumab plus semaglutide; preservation of clinically important muscle function still needs decisive validation. Proposed completion test: Regulatory approval of a muscle-preservation claim after a randomized trial of at least 500 adults over at least 52 weeks, showing ≥15% mean weight loss, ≥90% of lost weight attributable to fat, and prespecified preservation of MRI-measured muscle and strength against clinically justified noninferiority margins. Test set by: Proposed editorial test; regulators would determine the acceptable indication and functional endpoints. BELIEVE's composition endpoints are trial milestones, not an accepted regulatory definition of muscle preservation. Overlaps: END-05, ORT-06. Sources given: [BELIEVE randomized phase 2 publication](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04204-0.pdf) ; [Scholar Rock November 2026 programme and regulatory update](https://scholarrock.gcs-web.com/static-files/d095bef0-0511-454b-ad49-13d8ef6afbee).

page.title: Drug-induced fat loss with muscle and strength preservation
page.definition: Pharmacological treatment of obesity reduces body fat while preserving skeletal muscle mass and strength. Muscle preservation is established using measurements specific to skeletal muscle together with strength outcomes.

goal.need: FDA reports that fat accounts for 60–90% of weight reduction in pharmacological trials; accompanying lean-mass loss has generally not been considered adverse. Lean mass includes skeletal muscle, organs and body water. Preserving muscle and functional capacity is an explicit EASO treatment goal for older adults with obesity.

statements.body: European Association for the Study of Obesity
statements.quote: Primary therapeutic goals should focus on preserving muscle mass, maintaining functional capacity, and improving quality of life rather than on weight reduction alone.
statements.context: The position statement concerns obesity management in older adults.

statements.quote: safely preserve lean muscle mass as an adjunctive therapy in overweight and obese adults who are taking a GLP-1 RA.
statements.context: The stated objective of its randomized phase 2 apitegromab obesity study. GLP-1 receptor agonists are drugs that activate a hormone receptor involved in appetite regulation.

completion.title: FDA approves an obesity treatment with explicit skeletal-muscle and strength-preservation claims.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing approval for a drug or drug combination whose approved labeling explicitly establishes fat reduction with preservation of skeletal muscle mass and strength in the indicated population. Evidence supports the muscle and strength claims alongside weight-management efficacy and safety. Numerical efficacy thresholds, functional endpoints and acceptable preservation margins are those accepted by FDA for that indication.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; no published combined numerical completion test was located.
completion.basis: FDA and EMA weight-management guidance, EASO recommendations and Veru's disclosures of FDA feedback were searched for a combined fat-loss, muscle-mass and strength-preservation test. None was found. FDA places body-composition efficacy claims outside its draft's scope. Approval with explicit muscle and strength claims provides a verifiable fallback without assigning numerical efficacy or noninferiority margins.

milestones.title: An adjunct reduces lean-mass loss in obese mice receiving a GLP-1 receptor agonist.
milestones.criterion: A comparative experiment demonstrates less lean-mass loss with an adjunct than with the same GLP-1 treatment plus control antibody in diet-induced obese mice. On 6 February 2024, Scholar Rock reported lean-mass changes of −1.4% with its SRK-439 study antibody plus semaglutide versus −11.3% with control antibody plus semaglutide, with eight mice per group. Semaglutide was 0.04 mg/kg daily; the adjunct was 3 mg/kg weekly. Body composition was measured by quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance. The reported result was not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Scholar Rock, published comparative mouse experiment presented at Keystone Symposia on 5 February 2024; an experimental efficacy test.
milestones.threshold_quote: SRK-439 diminished the GLP-1 RA-driven lean mass loss

milestones.title: FDA permits clinical testing of a muscle-preserving obesity treatment after reviewing its IND.
milestones.criterion: FDA reviews the investigational new drug application, including supporting safety evidence and the proposed human study, and permits clinical testing. On 23 January 2024, Scholar Rock announced FDA clearance of its IND for a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 study of apitegromab in adults receiving GLP-1 therapy for obesity. This establishes permission to test the obesity indication; it does not establish treatment efficacy. The clearance is documented by a sponsor announcement.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, The FDA's Drug Review Process: Ensuring Drugs Are Safe and Effective, IND review stage.
milestones.threshold_quote: At this stage, the FDA decides whether it is reasonably safe for the company to move forward with testing the drug in humans.

milestones.title: Human dosing establishes tolerability and drug exposure sufficient for phase 2 testing.
milestones.criterion: Phase 1 establishes human pharmacokinetics, pharmacological effects and tolerability sufficient to design controlled phase 2 studies. Apitegromab's randomized phase 1 study included 66 healthy adults and ran from 27 April 2018 to 11 March 2019. Single and multiple intravenous doses up to 30 mg/kg were tolerated and produced sustained increases in circulating latent myostatin, a marker of binding to the intended target. The study supported development initially for spinal muscular atrophy; it did not test preservation during obesity treatment.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase I Clinical Studies; apitegromab provides a published human example.
milestones.threshold_quote: permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies.

milestones.title: An adult loses ≥10% of fat mass with <5% lean-mass loss at 48 weeks.
milestones.criterion: Individual responders have ≥10% reduction in total fat mass and <5% decrease or an increase in lean mass, measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, at 48 weeks. BELIEVE randomized 507 adults; 57 were assigned to the high-dose combination. Related 72-week efficacy estimates were −22.1% body weight, −45.7% fat mass and −2.9% lean mass during an open-label extension. The paper found no significant improvement in grip strength or patient-reported outcomes. These arm means do not establish the composite responder proportion.
milestones.set_by: Versanis Bio, an Eli Lilly subsidiary, BELIEVE protocol version 5.0, approved on 9 April 2024, Table 1. The threshold appears in a table and defines individual responders without a required response fraction.

milestones.title: An adjunct reduces the proportion of adults losing ≥10% stair-climb power at 16 weeks.
milestones.criterion: Veru's exploratory QUALITY analysis compares the proportion of adults with ≥10% decline from baseline in stair-climb power after 16 weeks of semaglutide plus adjunct versus semaglutide plus placebo. In 168 randomized adults aged ≥60 years, Veru reported a 59.8% relative reduction with enobosarm 3 mg, P=0.0006, in its filing dated 10 August 2026. This is sponsor-reported evidence, not peer reviewed; prespecification of the responder analysis was not verified.
milestones.set_by: Veru, published QUALITY functional responder analysis in its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 June 2026; a sponsor-defined analysis rule rather than an FDA efficacy threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: subjects that lost at least 10% stair climb power

milestones.title: Confirmatory trials establish efficacy and safety supporting muscle-preservation labeling.
milestones.criterion: Phase 3 studies establish the additional clinical effectiveness and safety evidence needed to evaluate the regimen's benefit–risk relationship and support its proposed labeling. For a body-composition efficacy claim, FDA's January 2025 draft calls for agreement on the clinical condition and endpoints measuring patient benefit. The general phase 3 standard supplies this stage; it supplies no numerical muscle- or strength-preservation margin. No qualifying confirmatory obesity result was located.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase 3 Clinical Studies, together with its January 2025 draft weight-reduction guidance.
milestones.threshold_quote: needed to evaluate the overall benefit-risk relationship of the drug.

not_found: No FDA, EMA or society document located defines a combined numerical threshold for fat loss, skeletal-muscle preservation and strength preservation.
No publicly available FDA feedback letter was found to independently verify Veru's account of its indication-specific regulatory advice.
The BELIEVE composite responder proportion was not located in the opened publication.
The ClinicalTrials.gov QUALITY page opened without study fields, preventing verification of its protocol and analysis plan.
No qualifying confirmatory obesity result or approved muscle-and-strength-preservation claim was located as of 15 November 2026.

results.finding: In diet-induced obese mice, semaglutide plus bimagrumab preserved lean mass; semaglutide plus control antibody reduced it by approximately 10% (n=8 and 9).
results.detail: The experiment used bimagrumab with semaglutide and recombinant IgG1 as the control antibody. Body composition was assessed by EchoMRI over 14 days.
results.quote: Daily treatment of obese mice with semaglutide potently decreased body weight; this included a significant decrease in both muscle and fat mass. Combination treatment with bimagrumab and semaglutide led to superior fat mass loss while simultaneously preserving lean mass despite reduced food intake.

results.finding: In 66 healthy adults, single and multiple apitegromab doses up to 30 mg/kg were tolerated and produced sustained target engagement.
results.detail: The study characterized pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics and informed phase 2 dosing for spinal muscular atrophy. It did not assess muscle preservation during obesity treatment.
results.quote: Single and multiple apitegromab doses resulted in dose-dependent and sustained increases in serum latent myostatin, indicating robust target engagement.
